Figure 1.6 box diagram: Original Complex Problem -> Divide into -> Small problem 1..4 -> Solution 1..4 -> Combining the solutions -> Complete Solution. pages.observations: Figure 2.2 Main steps involved in the implementation of water supply project, three rows of boxes: (1) Collection of data (Investigation and survey) -> Identify gaps in benchmarks and actual baseline performance -> Planning and development of water resources through IUWRM -> Ward-wise population forecast and demand estimation; (2) GIS based hydraulic model for transmission main and distribution system -> Quantity estimation and cost schedule -> Detailed Project Report (DPR) -> Invite tenders for execution of project; (3) Commissioning of project and then carry out Effective operations -> Effective O&M -> Management -> 24x7 System. pages.no_targets_reason: Sections 2.5 and 2.6 in prose only. NRW is defined in words, not as a displayed or inline symbolic formula, so there is no equation target; no table appears.
pages.observations: 2.5 Reduction of NRW strategy: NRW defined as 'the difference of the quantity of water supplied and water billed', comprising physical loss and commercial loss; 'more than 50%', 'Average NRW in Indian cities is 31%', 'reduced to 15% for overall system and 10% for distribution system at DMA level', 'not 100% metered', 'at least 10% of the customers', 'decreased to less than 15%'. Top-down and bottom-up water audit are described in words only: no equals sign, operator symbols or symbol definitions are printed, so no equation is drafted (writing 'NRW = supplied - billed' would be an invented formula, not a visual transcription). 2.6 Planning Objectives repeats the acronym in prose, printed '(IUWRM)' after 'Integrated Urban Water Resource Management', confirmed on a 4x crop (tmp/pdfs/water-a-t02/p106-iuwrm-zoom.png) - the same IUWRM spelling as the Figure 2.2 box on page 104, while page 97 prose prints IURWM; not corrected. Cites IS 10500:2012.
